notes: **Presenter:** Joshua. One person, one list, in video order.

**The numbers to match** (TQX's own test, `claims-and-proof` → "10 biggest US stocks"): AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL, META, TSLA, AVGO, JPM, BRK.B · buy at the close of a day one drops 3% or more · $2,000 per stock · sell at +3% from the buy or −5% · $10,000 start · no fees · Jan 2021 – Dec 2025 → **$18,147 (+$8,147) · 607 trades · worst drop −$3,207**.

open.text: **A real Qube run of this rule (A2, A3).** The numbers come from our own test, not from Qube yet. If Qube shows anything different, nothing gets filmed until Mark decides.
**Same rule and numbers as J018** (Day 1 of the paper-trading series, written, not filmed). Fine to share, but if both get filmed the numbers will look reused. Which one goes first?
**Hook A opens "Claude can now…", like J022's hook A.** It's the original's hook, so it stays (Mark's method). If J020 and J022 post close together, use hook B or C here.
**Paper trading isn't said out loud** (the original has no such line). The edit shows "BACKTEST ✓ → PAPER → LIVE" with "Go live" locked. OK as is, or add "then on paper" (+3 words, about 1s)?
**Length:** 155 words, about 48s at Joshua's pace (the original is 44s, the brief asks 44–48s). Old line 10 ("So you get to see all that…") is cut; the hook already makes that promise.

**CTA offer.** The original's CTA pays off its "all 11 skills" loop. Ours stays the approved line. If the DM ever sends this video's exact prompt (A1), the CTA could name it; until the flow sends it, no change.
**The Breakdown DM still isn't live in ManyChat.** The CTA promises a step-by-step; it has to be in the flow before posting.
**Target vs stop split:** if A3 shows it, add it to `claims-and-proof` first. Only then can it go into lines 8–9 as the honest version of their "29.4% hit target / 25.5% hit stop".

lines.text: Claude can now test your stock trade 10,000 times before you risk a single dollar.
Someone just open sourced 11 free day trading skills for Claude and each one handles a different job.
One skill scans thousands of stock charts looking for trading opportunities.
Another tracks breaking news that could move those stocks.
Then there's an entry skill that watches for the right signal and an exit skill that plans when to take profit or cut your losses.
But the craziest one is called the time machine.
It takes your trade and simulates the rest of the trading day 10,000 times using historical price data.
Then it shows how often you would have made money, hit your stop loss or ended somewhere in between.
So you get to see the historical odds before putting your money on the line.
Of course, it's a simulation, not a guarantee.
To get all 11 skills and the full setup guide, follow Build with AI and comment trade.
